name: Trial And Error

date.source: the show's own dateline, "Live On Pay Per View January 27th, 2002"

notes: BMW's own first held pay-per-view of the surviving record, from its earlier v1/v2 era (predating the version-3 relaunch's 'Withdrawn' branding). A companion hype/preview document (trial-and-error-hype.html) survives but carries no card information of its own — prose only, not structured here.

matches.note: Reality pinned Ace with a springboard moonsault after Ace's own five-star frog splash had put Orion away moments earlier.
Chilly K retained with a top-rope Frostbite after a back-and-forth match of repeated near-falls.

matches.stipulation: Welcome To Hell Match (Blood Money Title)
matches.note: A two-arena, four-key hardcore hunt across the building's own backstage areas and parking lot; Reaper's own estranged son Joseph Rice interfered against him but, in a scramble for the final key, ended up costing Van Helsing the win instead — Reaper locked in the Grim Demise for the finish.
The Underlord won the title with a top-rope chokeslam, "The Sacrifice."

Eiji Fujiwara subbed for Tycoon, who declined to wrestle his own team's spot. Fujiwara was pulled from ringside by a run-in from Ace partway through and never returned; Ice pinned Thee Obsession for the final fall.

eliminations.note: Dragon Suplex into a pinning combination.
Flying elbow off the top rope.

Pulled to ringside and brawled off through the crowd by a run-in from Ace (billed separately on this same card's own opening four-way, not an entrant of this match), removing him from the match without a fall.
Pinned after being softened up by Eiji Fujiwara's own Fujiwara Driver.
Ice Breaker, a powerbomb off the top rope — the match's own final fall.

matches.note: Donomite locked in a sharpshooter with a live microphone at Ragio Versace's mouth for the submission.

matches.stipulation: Asterdome Match, Best of 3 Falls (Million Dollar Title)
matches.note: Fall 1 (barbed-wire cage): Krazie. Fall 2 (TLC lumberjack): Teflon. Fall 3 (20-count last-man-standing around the set): Teflon, after throwing Krazie off the Money-Tron onto a platform below — Krazie left with a broken leg and, per later columns, his BMW career over.
A steel-cage main event; Axel Teflon kicked the cage door into Jeremiah Wilson's face as he tried to be the first out, letting Risk escape and win the title instead.

name: Money, Power, Respect II

date.source: the news item's own dateline (news-money-power-respect-2.html) and the column's own "July 28th, 2002" heading (columns.html)

notes: Structured from the fed's own "MPR Recap" column (one of several columns served together on columns.html); a second column on the same page, "A Krazie View," recaps the same card with some details that don't fully agree with the MPR Recap's own account (see the Krisis/Violent B/Tank/J-Man match note and the Blood Money Championship's own reign note). A separate announcement-only news item (news-money-power-respect-2.html) carries no card details of its own.

matches.stipulation: Non-Title Tag Match (per the MPR Recap column)
matches.note: J-Man turned on his own partner 'Tank' Hank Gunyon mid-match and pinned Krisis with a steel-chair shot, per the MPR Recap column's own blow-by-blow. The same page's separate 'A Krazie View' column instead lists "Winners: Tank & J-Man" and names Violent B the new Blood Money Champion "due to the attack of J-Man" — the two accounts on the same served page do not agree; see the Blood Money Championship's own reign note.

Paranoia won with the Careless Paranoia (reverse shooting star press into a pinfall) on Anthony Balboa. Newcomers 'The Violence' Vince Jones and Raymond Mercy both debuted immediately after, jumping Paranoia from behind and then each other.
The Rockweiler won by submission with the Weiler Hold (a sharpshooter).

matches.stipulation: Inferno Tables Tag Team Match (Tag Team Title, vacant)
matches.note: 2GLS (Reality and Jeremiah Wilson) sent Big Money Legends' Kid Krazie through three burning stacked tables with a double press slam for the win, awarded the previously-vacated Tag Team Championship.

A brawl that ran through the arena and a parking-lot truck chase; ICE's own ex-girlfriend Kelly threw a lit match onto him mid-pinfall, then struck him with his own title, letting Da Thug finish the cover.

Tax pinned Risk with the Stock Market Crash to win the title; champion Billy Blaze was not the man pinned but lost the belt regardless. 2GLS immediately jumped Tax afterward until an unbilled newcomer — later revealed as The British Bomber — ran them off.

name: FallOut: American Airlines Arena

date.source: Undated in the source; internal references place it after Trial And Error (27 Jan 2002) — the broadcast recaps that PPV's own Cruiserweight and World Title matches — and before the document's own 5 February 2002 capture.

notes: FallOut was one of two weekly shows (with SellOut) in BMW's earlier v1/v2 era, before the version-3 relaunch's single 'Withdrawn' broadcast.

matches.note: Chris Hyde rolled up Hector Capone for the win after Da Mab's own frog splash had put both Capone and Hyde down moments earlier.

Eiji Fujiwara won with the Fujiwara Driver; explicitly billed non-title, so Chilly K's Cruiserweight Championship was not on the line. Reality ran in and attacked Chilly K with a chair immediately after.
The SensationalSal One won by submission with the Brampton Cloverleaf.

Billed under his own second identity, 'Mafia Man' Mario Ghotti; commentary raised the Cash Money Championship by name but the match was never explicitly declared a title match, and no title change is announced afterward — recorded here as a non-title result. Reality rolled him up with a handful of tights for the win; Chilly K and Ghotti's own two bodyguards then beat Reality down after the bell.

name: FallOut: Ocean Center, Daytona Beach

date.source: Undated in the source; captured 5 February 2002, from the same v1/v2-era FallOut broadcast run as the American Airlines Arena card.

no_appearances_reason: A card only — no results page for this broadcast was captured. Every entrant is recorded as billed, not as having wrestled.

name: Withdrawn: Live on June 6th

date.source: the card's own "Live on June 6th" heading; year inferred from the document's own 5 June 2002 capture proximity

no_appearances_reason: A card only — no results page for this broadcast was captured. Every entrant is recorded as billed, not as having wrestled. A later column reports Brad Douglas's death by suicide on this same date; the surviving record does not reconcile that report with his own billing on this card.
